contract_deployer.title: Contract Deployer
contract_deployer.description: Deploy smart contracts deterministically using CREATE2 proxy
contract_deployer.feature_2: Same contract address on every network

faqs.create2_explanation: CREATE2 is an Ethereum opcode that allows deterministic contract deployment. It calculates the contract address before deployment based on bytecode and salt, ensuring the same address across different networks.
faqs.deterministic_explanation: Deterministic deployment means the contract will always be deployed to the same address on any network, as long as you use the same bytecode, constructor arguments, and salt. This is extremely useful for cross-chain applications.
faqs.bytecode_explanation: Bytecode is the compiled version of your smart contract code. When you compile your Solidity contract, you get bytecode which is the actual code that runs on the Ethereum Virtual Machine (EVM).
faqs.abi_explanation: ABI (Application Binary Interface) defines how to interact with your contract. For deployment, you need the constructor ABI to properly encode the constructor arguments. You can provide it in JSON format or human-readable format.
faqs.salt_explanation: Salt is a 32-byte value used in CREATE2 to generate the contract address. Different salts result in different addresses. You can use the same salt to deploy to the same address on different networks.

wallet_sweep.title: Wallet Sweep
wallet_sweep.description: Transfer balances from multiple wallets to one address
wallet_sweep.feature_1: Complete balance sweep, zero dust left
wallet_sweep.feature_3: No native token required in source wallets

faqs.network_explanation: A blockchain network is a public ledger system that records who owns what tokens and all transfers. Ethereum, BSC, and Polygon are different ledgers, each independent and separate.
faqs.wallet_explanation: A Web3 wallet isn't where money is stored - it's the key to manage your blockchain account. Your funds are recorded on the blockchain ledger, and the wallet proves you own the account. Popular: MetaMask, Coinbase Smart Wallet.
faqs.native_token_explanation: Native tokens are used to pay miners who process your transactions. Ethereum uses ETH, BSC uses BNB, Polygon uses POL. Miners record your transaction on the blockchain ledger, and you pay them this fee.
faqs.eip7702_explanation: Tech that temporarily upgrades regular wallets to smart contract wallets during a transaction. No extra deployment needed.
faqs.why_need_eip7702_explanation: Lets wallets with no gas money send tokens. Your main wallet pays gas for them, enabling one-click sweep.
faqs.create2_proxy_explanation: Deployment tool ensuring same contract address across all chains. Same code = same address everywhere.
faqs.multicall3_explanation: Batches multiple calls into one. Saves gas and time. All-or-nothing execution.
faqs.biubiu_premium_explanation: Membership contract managing subscriptions, discounts, and access. Fully open source.
faqs.wallet_sweep_explanation: Core contract for batch transfers. Handles EIP-7702 delegation and approvals. Open source: https://github.com/atshelchin/biubiu-contracts
faqs.can_select_multiple_tokens: Can I select multiple tokens at once?
faqs.can_select_multiple_tokens_explanation: Yes! You can select as many tokens as you want. The tool will sweep all selected tokens in one batch operation, making it very efficient.
faqs.what_happens_zero_balance: What happens if a wallet has zero balance for a token?
faqs.what_happens_zero_balance_explanation: Smart! The system automatically skips wallets with zero balance for that specific token. This saves you gas costs by not executing unnecessary transfers.
faqs.what_tokens_supported: What types of tokens are supported?
faqs.what_tokens_supported_explanation: We support both native tokens (like ETH on Ethereum, BNB on BSC, MATIC on Polygon) and all ERC-20 standard tokens. Most tokens you encounter will work.
faqs.how_add_custom_token: How do I add a custom token?
faqs.how_add_custom_token_explanation: Click the '+ Add Token' button, then enter the token's contract address. The system will automatically fetch the token's name, symbol, and decimals from the blockchain.

faqs.custom_amounts_explanation: In custom amounts mode, you can specify different amounts for each recipient. This is useful when different addresses should receive different quantities.
faqs.how_to_import_recipients: How can I import recipient addresses?

faqs.networks_supported_explanation: Currently we support Ethereum Mainnet, Polygon, BSC (Binance Smart Chain), Base, Arbitrum, and Optimism. More networks will be added in the future.

faqs.balance_checker_explanation: A tool to scan multiple wallet addresses and check their token balances. It helps you quickly identify which wallets have assets and aggregate total holdings across all wallets.
faqs.how_many_addresses: How many addresses can I scan at once?
faqs.how_many_addresses_explanation: You can scan up to 100,000 wallet addresses in a single batch. The tool uses optimized RPC calls to efficiently query balances.
faqs.what_tokens_supported: What types of tokens are supported?
faqs.what_tokens_supported_explanation: We support native tokens (ETH, BNB, MATIC, etc.) and all ERC-20 standard tokens. You can add any token by entering its contract address.
faqs.is_it_free_explanation: Yes! Balance scanning is completely free and requires no on-chain transactions. It only reads data from the blockchain.
faqs.multicall_explanation: Multicall3 is a smart contract that batches multiple read calls into one request. This dramatically speeds up scanning by reducing the number of RPC calls needed.
faqs.can_export_results: Can I export the scan results?
faqs.can_export_explanation: Yes! You can export results to CSV or JSON format for further analysis in spreadsheets or other tools.
faqs.networks_supported_explanation: We support Ethereum, Polygon, BSC, Base, Arbitrum, and Optimism. You can also add custom EVM-compatible networks.

faqs.subtitle: Everything you need to know about biubiu.tools

items.question: What is biubiu.tools?
items.answer: biubiu.tools is a comprehensive Web3 toolkit that provides batch operations and multi-wallet management features for the Ethereum ecosystem.

items.question: Is it safe to use?
items.answer: Yes! We never store your private keys. All operations are performed locally in your browser using secure Web3 protocols.

items.question: Which chains are supported?
items.answer: We support Ethereum mainnet and major EVM-compatible chains including Polygon, BSC, Arbitrum, and Optimism.

items.question: How does batch wallet collection work?
items.answer: Our tool allows you to collect tokens from multiple wallets to a single address in one transaction, saving time and gas fees.

items.question: Can I try it for free?
items.answer: Absolutely! Our free plan includes basic features with up to 10 wallets. You can upgrade anytime for more advanced features.
